slides.title: What is an API? The Restaurant Waiter Analogy
slides.narration:
Have you ever wondered how different apps talk to each other?
Or how an app gets information from a large **AI** model?
Imagine you are at a restaurant.
You want to order some food, right?
You don't go into the kitchen yourself to tell the chef.
Instead, you tell the waiter what you want.
The waiter takes your order to the kitchen.
The chef prepares the food.
Then, the waiter brings the food back to you.
In this scenario, the waiter is like an **API**.
An **API**, or **Application Programming Interface**, is a messenger.
It allows different software applications to communicate.
It takes your request and delivers it to another system.
Then, it brings the response back to you.
This is how your apps can use powerful **AI** models.
Without an **API**, every app would need its own kitchen.
